name: Aspen Snowmass
fact: Four mountains on one ticket; Snowmass alone drops 4,406 ft, the most vertical in the US.

name: Jackson Hole
fact: Home of Corbet's Couloir, and a tram that climbs 4,139 ft in nine minutes.

name: Zermatt
fact: A car-free village under the Matterhorn; Europe's highest lift tops out at 3,883 m.

name: Chamonix
fact: Hosted the very first Winter Olympics, in 1924, under Mont Blanc.

name: St. Moritz
fact: Hosted the Winter Olympics twice (1928 and 1948) and claims to have invented winter tourism in 1864.

name: Deer Valley
fact: Skiers only: snowboards have been banned since it opened in 1981.

name: Palisades Tahoe
fact: Hosted the 1960 Winter Olympics as Squaw Valley; renamed in 2021.

name: Mammoth
fact: One of the longest seasons in North America, regularly skiing into June and occasionally August.

name: Steamboat
fact: Trademarked the phrase 'Champagne Powder' for its famously light, dry snow.

name: Big Sky
fact: The Lone Peak tram tops out at 11,166 ft; 5,850 acres makes it one of the biggest in America.

name: Alta
fact: Skiers only since 1938, and averages over 500 inches of snow a year.

name: Snowbird
fact: The Aerial Tram rises 2,900 ft to Hidden Peak, and the season often runs into May.

name: Sun Valley
fact: America's first destination ski resort (1936), and home of the world's first chairlift.

name: Kitzbühel
fact: Hosts the Hahnenkamm, the most feared downhill race on the World Cup.

name: Lake Louise
fact: Sits inside Banff National Park, Canada's oldest national park.

name: Niseko United
fact: Around 15 metres of snow a year, blown in from Siberia across the Sea of Japan.

name: Killington
fact: 'The Beast of the East': six peaks and the longest season on the East Coast.

name: Banff Sunshine
fact: Straddles the Continental Divide, so you can ski from Alberta into British Columbia.

name: Tremblant
fact: Opened in 1939 and is the biggest ski area in eastern Canada.

name: Dolomiti Superski
fact: Twelve ski areas and 1,200 km of runs in a UNESCO World Heritage mountain range.

name: Copper Mountain
fact: The terrain sorts itself naturally: easiest runs on the west side, hardest on the east.

name: Winter Park
fact: Owned by the City of Denver, and reachable on the Winter Park Express ski train.

name: Revelstoke
fact: North America's biggest lift-served vertical: 5,620 ft.

name: Taos
fact: Skiers-only for decades; snowboarders were finally allowed in 2008.

name: Arapahoe Basin
fact: 'The Legend': one of the highest ski areas in the US, with lifts above 13,000 ft.

name: Brighton
fact: Utah's oldest ski resort, started in 1936 with a rope tow made from an old elevator cable.

name: Solitude
fact: Big Cottonwood Canyon's quieter mountain, with over 500 inches of snow a year.

name: Snowbasin
fact: Hosted the downhill and super-G races at the 2002 Winter Olympics.

name: Sugarloaf
fact: The only lift-served above-treeline skiing in the East, on Maine's second-highest peak.

name: Sunday River
fact: Eight interconnected peaks across three miles of western Maine.

name: Stratton
fact: Where Jake Burton tested his boards; in 1983 it became the first major resort to allow snowboarding.

name: Sugarbush
fact: Two mountains, Lincoln Peak and Mount Ellen, joined by the two-mile Slide Brook Express.

name: Crystal Mountain
fact: Washington's largest ski area, with Mount Rainier filling the view from the top.

name: Mt. Bachelor
fact: A volcano: you can ski 360 degrees around the summit cone.

name: Big Bear Mountain Resort
fact: Two mountains, Bear Mountain and Snow Summit, two hours from Los Angeles.

name: Courmayeur
fact: The Italian side of Mont Blanc, linked to Chamonix by a tunnel through the mountain.

name: Cervinia
fact: Shares the Matterhorn's lifts with Zermatt; the Swiss border runs across the top.

name: Hakuba Valley
fact: Ten resorts in the Japanese Alps; hosted the alpine events of the 1998 Nagano Olympics.

name: Thredbo
fact: Home to Australia's longest ski runs, inside Kosciuszko National Park.

name: Snowshoe
fact: An upside-down mountain: the village sits on top and you ski down to the lifts.

name: Red Mountain
fact: Skied since 1897, and in 2016 it sold shares in itself to the public.

name: Schweitzer
fact: Idaho's largest ski area, looking out over Lake Pend Oreille.

name: Grandvalira
fact: The biggest resort in the Pyrenees, with 210 km of runs across Andorra.

name: Valle Nevado
fact: The largest ski area in South America, 46 km from Santiago; the season is July and August.

name: Coronet Peak / The Remarkables
fact: Queenstown's two mountains; the Remarkables stood in for Middle-earth in The Lord of the Rings.

name: Loon
fact: New Hampshire's busiest mountain, two hours from Boston.

name: June Mountain
fact: Mammoth's quieter sister, twenty minutes up the road.

name: Windham
fact: In the Catskills, two and a half hours from New York City.

name: Mt. Norquay
fact: Banff's local hill since 1926, and home of Canada's first chairlift (1948).

name: Sun Peaks
fact: Canada's second-largest ski area; Olympic champion Nancy Greene is its director of skiing.

name: Panorama
fact: One of Canada's biggest verticals, 4,265 ft, in the Purcell Mountains.

name: SilverStar
fact: A Victorian-style village painted in bright colours, above Vernon, BC.

name: Eldora
fact: Boulder's local hill, 21 miles from town and served by a public bus.

name: Summit at Snoqualmie
fact: Four ski areas on one pass, less than an hour from Seattle.

name: Alpental
fact: The steep, expert side of Snoqualmie Pass.

name: Mt. Buller
fact: Three hours from Melbourne, the closest major resort to a big Australian city.

name: Mt. Hutt
fact: One of the longest seasons in the Southern Hemisphere, an hour from Christchurch.

name: Cypress Mountain
fact: Hosted the freestyle skiing and snowboarding at the 2010 Vancouver Olympics.

name: Blue Mountain (Ontario)
fact: Ontario's biggest resort, on the Niagara Escarpment above Georgian Bay.

name: Pico
fact: Opened in 1937, and its 1940 T-bar was the first in America.

name: Boyne Mountain
fact: Michigan's first chairlift, bought second-hand from Sun Valley in 1948.

name: The Highlands
fact: Formerly Boyne Highlands, in the lake-effect snowbelt of northern Michigan.

name: Camelback
fact: In the Poconos, 90 minutes from New York, with a water park at the base.

name: Blue Mountain (PA)
fact: Pennsylvania's biggest vertical drop, 1,082 ft.

name: Lee Canyon
fact: A ski area 45 minutes from the Las Vegas Strip.

name: Jiminy Peak
fact: The first ski resort in North America to power itself with its own wind turbine.

name: Lotte Arai
fact: Reopened in 2017 after a decade shut; famous for deep Niigata powder.

name: Monterosa (Champoluc)
fact: Three valleys linked beneath Monte Rosa, the Alps' second-highest massif.

name: Pila
fact: Reached by gondola straight up from the city of Aosta.

name: La Thuile
fact: Linked across the French border with La Rosière.

name: Lutsen Mountains
fact: The Midwest's biggest ski area, on the north shore of Lake Superior.

name: Granite Peak
fact: Wisconsin's biggest vertical, on Rib Mountain, a state park near Wausau.

name: Snowriver
fact: Two former rivals, Blackjack and Indianhead, now one resort in Michigan's Upper Peninsula.
